feed.title: Chapter 4: Computer Vision & CNNs — Civil Engineer's Guide to AI
feed.subtitle: Updates to Chapter 4 sub-lessons.

entry.title: 4.1 Images as Data
entry.summary: Understand how computers see images as numerical data. Explore pixels, grayscale vs color, RGB channels, resolution, and image tensors through a civil engineering lens with interactive demos.

entry.title: 4.2 Convolution Operation
entry.summary: Learn the convolution operation: sliding kernels over images, element-wise multiplication and summation, padding, stride, and common filters like Sobel edge detection. Interactive demos with civil engineering examples.

entry.title: 4.3 Pooling & Stride
entry.summary: Understand pooling layers (max, average, global average) and stride as a downsampling alternative. Interactive demos with civil engineering examples: reducing drone image features while preserving crack information.

entry.title: 4.4 CNN Architecture
entry.summary: Build a complete CNN architecture: stacking convolutional layers, pooling, flatten, fully connected layers, ReLU, softmax, batch normalization, dropout, receptive fields, and feature hierarchy. Interactive CNN builder and feature hierarchy visualizer for crack classification.

entry.title: 4.5 Training CNNs
entry.summary: How to train Convolutional Neural Networks: forward pass, loss computation, backpropagation, weight update, data augmentation for civil engineering imagery, transfer learning for crack detection, learning rate scheduling, and batch size effects. Interactive data augmentation gallery and training progress monitor.

entry.title: 4.6 Famous CNN Architectures
entry.summary: A tour of landmark CNN architectures from LeNet-5 (1998) to EfficientNet: AlexNet, VGG, GoogLeNet/Inception, ResNet, DenseNet, and MobileNet. Key innovations, civil engineering relevance, interactive architecture timeline, and residual connection visualizer.

entry.title: 4.7 Object Detection
entry.summary: From image classification to object detection: anchor boxes, IoU, Non-Maximum Suppression, mAP, two-stage vs one-stage detectors (R-CNN family, YOLO, SSD). Interactive IoU calculator and NMS visualizer. Civil engineering applications for crack detection, spalling, rebar exposure, and safety equipment monitoring.

entry.title: 4.8 Semantic Segmentation
entry.summary: Pixel-level classification with encoder-decoder architectures, FCN, U-Net skip connections, transposed convolution, dice loss, and IoU per class. Civil engineering applications for crack segmentation, damage mapping, and road surface analysis. Interactive segmentation painter and U-Net architecture diagram.

entry.title: 4.9 Visualizing CNN Internals
entry.summary: Explore CNN interpretability techniques including feature map visualization, filter visualization, Grad-CAM, saliency maps, occlusion sensitivity, and t-SNE for civil engineering applications. Understand what a crack detector sees and build trust in AI for structural assessment.

entry.title: 4.10 CE Case Study: Crack Detection
entry.summary: End-to-end case study building a CNN-based crack detection system for concrete infrastructure. Covers dataset preparation, ResNet-18 transfer learning, training, evaluation with confusion matrix and ROC curves, Grad-CAM validation, and edge deployment on inspection drones.
